newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile likely to relax rates in early 1997 - Massad.
newsitem.headline: Chile likely to relax rates in early 1997 - Massad.

text.p: Chile's Central Bank will relax interest rates "when it becomes necessary," probably in the first half of 1997, Central Bank President Carlos Massad said.
Massad said the bank will end its restrictive monetary policy, known as the adjustment, as soon as the economy gives signs that the adjustment has succeeded, he said.
The Central Bank "will end the adjustement when it becomes necessary," he told reporters after meeting Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat.
"Our vision is that that will happen in the first half of next year," he said.

Chile's Central Bank has pursued a tight monetary policy most of this year in efforts to diminsh inflation, cutting economic growth to a project seven percent this year after over eight percent growth last year.
